Global Circles is Soliya's open-enrolment virtual exchange. Each round brings together hundreds of participants who are placed into small groups of about 15 people, balanced across countries, backgrounds and viewpoints, and each group is guided by a professional facilitator.

The Junior Academy is the New York Academy of Sciences' signature high-school programme. Accepted students join Launchpad, an online platform where they form international teams and work on Innovation Challenges sponsored by companies, guided by STEM mentors. Each challenge starts with a kick-off week on research methods, design thinking and data analysis.

It is completely free, fully online and in English, and admission is selective (thousands apply from all over the world). A strong application in English is essential.

about.en:
Cubes in Space describes itself as the only global STEM programme giving students aged 11–18 suborbital flight opportunities on NASA missions. Students, usually guided by a teacher, design and build an experiment that fits inside a small cube, which is launched on a sounding rocket or research balloon from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility. Since 2014 around 28,000 students from 79 countries have taken part.

The programme includes an online student academy with learning modules, and selected experiments fly in summer and are returned to the teams for analysis. Registration and enrolment for 2026–27 open on 9 November 2026; the detailed timeline is on the official site. Note: the programme does not fly cubesats or nanosats.

Week one (2–6 November 2026) has subject webinars from the University's six academic schools, from Arts and Humanities to Clinical Medicine, each a short presentation followed by Q&A with academics. Week two (9–13 November) covers the Colleges, funding opportunities and student support.

There are over 100 live sessions; you book the ones you want, and recordings are available to all registered attendees afterwards. It is the best single way for international applicants to research Cambridge Master's and PhD courses and scholarships (such as Gates Cambridge and Cambridge Trust awards) before the main funding deadlines.

Free, with recordings for registrants

about.en:
The Global Sustainability Challenge (GSC) is an annual Stanford University initiative, run with a collective of leading universities (including HKUST, IIT Bombay, TUM and UNESP), in which university students design, build and showcase real-world sustainability solutions. Season 1 drew 3,000+ students from 90+ countries. In 2026–27 there are two themes: Sustainable Energy (generation, storage, access, efficiency, microgrids) and Adaptation & Resilience (water, food and heat resilience).

Teams of 1–6 undergraduate, graduate or PhD students, from any discipline and any country (teams can mix universities and countries), move through three phases: Ignite (team up, research and design, until 22 November 2026), Build (prototype and test, December 2026 – 22 February 2027) and Shine (regional finals in February–March 2027 and a Global Finale in Hangzhou, China, on 20–21 May 2027). Mentors, workshops and judges' feedback are built in; the prize pool is USD 35,000+, and winners may join Stanford's EcoGlobal ecopreneurship programme.

about.en:
Battlecode is a real-time strategy game for which teams write an autonomous program: two teams of virtual robots manage resources and execute offensive strategies against each other, and your code must coordinate the whole army. It is run by MIT students and has been a famous MIT programming tradition for decades.

The competition takes place throughout January, with lectures, sprint tournaments and qualifying tournaments online, ending in a final tournament. Anyone may participate and any team can win the sprint prizes; the main prizes are for student teams, including non-MIT and high-school teams (Battlecode 2026 paid out over USD 20,000 in prizes, with dedicated high-school awards).

24 Pull Requests is a long-running community project encouraging people to give back to open source during December. From 1 to 24 December you aim to send a pull request (or other contribution such as documentation, design, triage or user support) to open-source projects each day; the site suggests beginner-friendly projects and tracks your contributions.

More than 27,000 organisations have been involved. It is free, informal and ideal for students who want to practise Git and GitHub, collaborate with maintainers and strengthen their CV before applying to programmes such as Google Summer of Code or Outreachy. Organisers can also host local 24 Pull Requests hack events.

summary.ar: زمالة عبر الإنترنت يعمل فيها شباب من 16 إلى 24 عامًا من دول مختلفة في فرق على مهمة حقيقية لمنظمة غير ربحية، مع تدريب أسبوعي ومدرّب مرافق. تشارك نصف كل دفعة على الأقل بمساعدة مالية.

about.en:
Village Virtual Impact Lab is a fellowship run by Global Nomads Group, a nonprofit that has designed virtual cross-cultural programmes for young people since 1998. Each cycle has 32 fellows working in teams of eight from different countries; each team receives a brief from a real mission-driven NGO (environment, human rights, health, education and more), builds what it needs and presents it to the client.

The programme runs for 16 weeks from January 2027, with a live two-hour session most Saturdays (training workshops and team work) plus 2–4 hours of independent work per week, coaching from a Global Nomads coach, a certificate and letters on completion. Acceptance is selective (around 10% in past cohorts) but based on motivation rather than grades. It was designed for unstable internet and is accessible to neurodivergent learners and people with disabilities.

en: Real NGO project with an international team
Weekly live training and a personal coach
Financial aid for at least half of fellows (incl. devices/internet)

eligibility.en: Young people aged 16–24 (as of January 2027) anywhere in the world. No experience needed; English is the working language.

en: Open the Village page and start the application
Complete the written part and record a short video
Request financial aid in the application if needed
Submit by 7 Dec 2026 (rolling review)

costs.en: USD 3,500 for the full 16 weeks (training, coaching, certificate). Financial aid is available and can cover the full cost, devices and internet.

score_reason: Strong international online fellowship with generous aid; deadline soon

summary.ka: უფასო 5-კვირიანი ვირტუალური გაცვლა, რომელიც ინგლისურს, არაბულს ან ესპანურს შემსწავლელ საშუალო და უფროსი კლასების მოსწავლეებს უცხოელ თანატოლებთან აკავშირებს ახალგაზრდების მიერ შექმნილი მოდულებითა და ლაივ ორენოვანი სესიებით. კლასს მასწავლებელი არეგისტრირებს.
summary.ar: تبادل افتراضي مجاني لمدة 5 أسابيع يربط صفوف المرحلتين المتوسطة والثانوية التي تتعلم الإنجليزية أو العربية أو الإسبانية بأقران في الخارج عبر وحدات أعدّها شباب وجلسات مباشرة ثنائية اللغة. يسجّل المعلم الصف.

about.en:
Global Nomads Group's Building Understanding through Language Learning programme is a virtual exchange for middle- and high-school students learning English, Arabic or Spanish. Two tracks exist: English–Arabic and English–Spanish. Students complete four short self-paced modules built by young people (story exchanges, multimedia, real-life language) and join two live, facilitated bilingual sessions where they practise with peers who speak the language they are learning.

It lasts five weeks (about 4 hours of modules and 2 hours of live events), fits into normal class time, and students earn a certificate of completion. Teachers receive training and technical support, and the schedule is arranged with them. It is a natural fit for Arabic-speaking schools whose students are learning English.

en: Free for schools
Live bilingual sessions with peers abroad
Certificate for students

eligibility.en: Middle- and high-school classes learning English, Arabic or Spanish; a teacher must register the class.

en: Ask your English/Arabic/Spanish teacher to open the programme page
Teacher registers the class with the free form
Attend the orientation and schedule sessions with Global Nomads staff
Complete the modules and the two live exchanges

score_reason: Free and relevant for Arabic/English learners, but needs a teacher to sign up

summary.en: Online version of one of the largest university-run high-school maths contests, organised by Stanford students and open to middle- and high-school students anywhere in the world.
summary.ka: სტენფორდის სტუდენტების მიერ ორგანიზებული ერთ-ერთი უდიდესი საუნივერსიტეტო მათემატიკური ტურნირის ონლაინ ვერსია, ღია მსოფლიოს ნებისმიერი კუთხის საშუალო და უფროსი კლასების მოსწავლეებისთვის.
summary.ar: النسخة الإلكترونية لإحدى أكبر بطولات الرياضيات المدرسية التي تنظمها الجامعات، يديرها طلاب ستانفورد ومفتوحة لطلاب المرحلتين المتوسطة والثانوية من أي مكان في العالم.

about.en:
The Stanford Math Tournament (SMT) is run entirely by Stanford students, with support from the Stanford Undergraduate Mathematics Organization and the Department of Mathematics, and had over 2,000 participants globally in 2025. The in-person contest on Stanford's campus is for around 800 US students.

To widen access, SMT also hosts an online tournament, similar to the in-person contest, shortly after the April event; it is open to all middle- and high-school students from anywhere in the world. Past problems are on the website and are excellent olympiad training.

en: Run by Stanford students
Open to students worldwide online
Past problems available for practice

eligibility.en: Middle- and high-school students anywhere in the world.

en: Check stanfordmathtournament.com in early 2027
Register for the online tournament when it opens
Practise with past SMT problems
Compete online on the tournament day

costs.en: No fee is stated for the online tournament on the official site; check when registration opens.

score_reason: Respected contest with a global online edition; 2027 date TBC

summary.en: Five-week asynchronous course from Soliya, a leader in virtual exchange, teaching the foundations of facilitating dialogue across differences online, with individual feedback and two optional live sessions.
summary.ka: Soliya-ს, ვირტუალური გაცვლის ერთ-ერთი ლიდერის, ხუთკვირიანი ასინქრონული კურსი, რომელიც ონლაინ განსხვავებულ ადამიანებს შორის დიალოგის ფასილიტაციის საფუძვლებს ასწავლის, ინდივიდუალური უკუკავშირითა და ორი არასავალდებულო ლაივ სესიით.
summary.ar: دورة غير متزامنة لمدة خمسة أسابيع من Soliya، الرائدة في التبادل الافتراضي، تعلّم أسس تيسير الحوار عبر الإنترنت بين أشخاص مختلفين، مع ملاحظات فردية وجلستين مباشرتين اختياريتين.

about.en:
Soliya's Introduction to Online Dialogue Facilitation is the first step of its facilitator pathway. Over five weeks (11 January – 15 February 2027) and about 12–15 hours, participants study the functions of dialogue and facilitation, online group management and a foundational facilitation toolbox, with weekly assignments, individual feedback on their own facilitation profile and two optional live sessions.

Graduates can continue to Soliya's Advanced Facilitation Training and practicum, which leads to certification and paid facilitation opportunities in Soliya's virtual exchange programmes. It suits university students interested in conflict resolution, education, international relations or community work.

en: Self-paced, with weekly deadlines
Individual feedback on your facilitation style
Pathway to certification and paid facilitation work

eligibility.en: Adults (18+) from any country with good English. (A separate Arabic course, Virtu-PEACE, is limited to residents of certain countries.)

en: Open the Facilitation Training page
Register for the English course before 8 Jan 2027
Pay the training fee (bundle discounts available)
Complete the weekly modules from 11 Jan 2027

costs.en: Training fee USD 450; bundle discounts for multiple trainings.

score_reason: Quality skills course with set dates; paid

summary.ka: ათკვირიანი ლაივ ონლაინ ტრენინგი მცირე საერთაშორისო ჯგუფებში, სადაც მონაწილეები Soliya-ს ტრენერებთან ერთად დიალოგის ფასილიტაციას ვარჯიშობენ და Soliya-ს სერტიფიკატს იღებენ, რაც ანაზღაურებადი ფასილიტატორის როლისკენ გზას ხსნის.
summary.ar: تدريب مباشر عبر الإنترنت لمدة عشرة أسابيع في مجموعات دولية صغيرة يتدرّب فيه المشاركون على تيسير الحوار مع مدربي Soliya ويحصلون على شهادة Soliya، ما يفتح الباب لأدوار تيسير مدفوعة.

about.en:
Soliya's Advanced Facilitation Training is a 10-week live programme (also offered in a 5-week format) in which small, diverse cohorts work closely with Soliya trainers on Zoom, with asynchronous materials on Brightspace. Participants practise facilitation in real time, receive extensive individual feedback and build skills in active listening, handling difficult dynamics and group collaboration.

The spring 2027 round runs 15 March – 20 May 2027 (register by 24 February). Completion earns a Soliya certificate and is required for certification; certified facilitators can join Soliya's Community of Practice and become eligible for paid facilitation in its virtual exchange programmes.

en: Live practice in small international cohorts
Soliya certificate on completion
Route to paid facilitation work

eligibility.en: Adults (18+) from any country; completion of the introductory course or equivalent facilitation experience is expected.

en: Complete the introductory course (or show prior facilitation experience)
Register for the spring round before 24 Feb 2027
Pay the training fee (bundles available)
Join the weekly live sessions from 15 Mar 2027

costs.en: Paid training (see price plans and bundles on the official page).

score_reason: Professional-level facilitation training with certification; paid

summary.en: Apple's annual coding challenge for students worldwide: build an original interactive app playground in Swift. Winners receive Apple prizes and recognition, and Distinguished Winners are invited to Apple's developer conference.
summary.ka: Apple-ის ყოველწლიური პროგრამირების გამოწვევა მსოფლიოს სტუდენტებისთვის: შექმენი ორიგინალური ინტერაქტიული app playground Swift-ზე. გამარჯვებულები Apple-ის პრიზებსა და აღიარებას იღებენ, საუკეთესოები კი Apple-ის დეველოპერთა კონფერენციაზე მიიწვევიან.
summary.ar: تحدٍّ برمجي سنوي من Apple للطلاب حول العالم: ابنِ تطبيق app playground تفاعليًا أصليًا بلغة Swift. يحصل الفائزون على جوائز وتقدير من Apple، ويُدعى المتميزون منهم إلى مؤتمر Apple للمطورين.

about.en:
The Swift Student Challenge invites students to create an original app playground in Swift (in Swift Playgrounds or Xcode) that can be experienced in about three minutes. Submissions are judged on innovation, creativity, social impact and inclusivity; Apple selects winners and, from them, Distinguished Winners who have been invited to Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference.

You must enter as an individual, and you can win up to three times. The challenge runs every year with a submission window usually in February, so the months before are the time to learn Swift and build your project using Apple's free resources on the 'Get ready' page.

en: Free, individual entry from most countries
Winners recognised by Apple; top entries invited to WWDC
Great portfolio project for CS applicants

eligibility.en: Students who meet the minimum age for their country (13+ in most countries; 14–16+ in some, e.g. 16+ in Germany and the Netherlands), are registered as (free) Apple developers, and are enrolled in school, university, a STEM curriculum, or recently graduated. Not open to full-time employed developers.

en: Register for a free Apple developer account
Learn Swift with Apple's free resources and plan your idea
Build your app playground (individual work only)
Submit during the official 2027 window and answer the written prompts

costs.en: Free. A Mac or iPad helps for building in Swift Playgrounds/Xcode.

deadline_note: Annual cycle. In 2026 the season opened 15 Dec 2025, applications closed 14 Jan 2026, work ran 23 Jan – 20 Mar. The 2027 season follows the same pattern; check the official timeline.

summary.en: KDE's yearly mentorship programme, similar to Google Summer of Code: contributors anywhere work with a mentor on a code or non-code project for KDE's open-source software from January to March.
summary.ka: KDE-ის ყოველწლიური მენტორობის პროგრამა, Google Summer of Code-ის მსგავსი: ნებისმიერი ქვეყნის მონაწილეები იანვრიდან მარტამდე მენტორთან ერთად KDE-ის ღია კოდის პროგრამებისთვის კოდის ან არაკოდის პროექტზე მუშაობენ.
summary.ar: برنامج الإرشاد السنوي من KDE، على غرار Google Summer of Code: يعمل مساهمون من أي مكان مع مرشد على مشروع برمجي أو غير برمجي لبرمجيات KDE المفتوحة المصدر من يناير إلى مارس.

about.en:
Season of KDE (SoK) has run every year since 2013. It is similar to, but less formal than, Google Summer of Code: anyone can propose a code or non-code project (documentation, translation, design, promotion) from KDE's ideas list, or suggest their own idea after finding a mentor through KDE's mailing lists and Matrix channels.

The 2027 season is expected to follow the usual timeline: opening in mid-December, contributor applications closing in mid-January, about ten weeks of mentored work from late January to March, and certificates for successful contributors. It is free and a respected stepping stone towards GSoC and open-source careers.

en: Mentored open-source project
Code and non-code projects
Certificate for successful contributors

eligibility.en: Open to everyone (students especially welcome) from any country; good English for communicating with mentors.

en: Read the ideas page for the 2027 season
Contact a mentor and start contributing early
Submit your proposal before the application deadline (mid-January)
Work on your project with your mentor from late January

score_reason: Good free mentorship; 2027 dates follow the annual pattern
